newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares recover, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares recover, further gains seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.73 percent on Wednesday as investors snapped up stock on weakness.
The SBI index ended 22.18 points higher at 1,303.68. Since the start of the week it has added on 2.3 percent.

"Obviously investors regarded prices as low enough to start buying. If similar demand continues until the end of the week maybe we can say our market has finally picked up," said Jernej Obed, a trader at A bank.
"This could be the beginning of a rising trend, but the first swallow does not always mean the advent of spring," he added.
The SPI had fallen over 20 percent since February 11 when the central bank restricted international investors' access to the market by ordering them to open special custody accounts.

"When foreigners start buying again I expect the shares of pharmaceutical and food companies will perform as well as they did before the slowdown," said Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
Overall 11 shares rose, five fell and two were flat, while eight were untraded. Turnover jumped to 93.9 million tolars from 45.6 million.
"Prices and volumes are most likely to rise until the end of the week," Brankovic said.
SKB bank was the most actively traded share, firming 2.54 percent to 50,500 tolars on volume of 994 shares for total turnover of 49.9 million tolars.
Bank UBK was the biggest gainer, jumping 9.09 percent to 6,000 tolars on volume of 560 shares.
Bank Probanka led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.24 percent to 19,060 tolars on volume of 209 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
